🏆 Top Exam Strategies
1. Active Recall – test yourself, don't just re-read
2. Spaced Repetition – review after 1, 3, 7, 14 days
3. Past Papers – do last 5 years minimum
4. Pomodoro – 25 min study + 5 min break
5. Mind Maps – visual revision
📌 Sleep 8 hrs before exam — memory consolidates during sleep!

📅 How to Make a Study Plan
1. List all subjects + chapters
2. Mark exam dates on calendar
3. Assign 2–3 subjects/day (rotate)
4. Hard subjects → morning (peak focus)
5. Revision day every Sunday
💡 Tell me your grade + subjects + exam date → I'll guide your plan!

💪 Stay Motivated!
🎯 Set small daily goals (not weekly)
📱 Phone in another room while studying
🏅 Reward yourself after each session
👥 Study group = accountability
🌟 Remember WHY you're studying — your future self will thank you!

📐 Pythagoras Theorem
a² + b² = c²
c = hypotenuse (longest side)
✅ Example: a=3, b=4 → c=√(9+16)=5
📌 Only works for right-angled triangles!

📐 Quadratic Formula
x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac)) / 2a
For: ax² + bx + c = 0
✅ x²−5x+6=0 → x=2 or x=3
🔑 Discriminant (b²−4ac):
+ve → 2 real roots | 0 → 1 root | −ve → no real roots

💰 Simple Interest
SI = (P × R × T) / 100
P=Principal, R=Rate%, T=Time(years)
✅ P=5000, R=8%, T=3 → SI = ₹1200
Amount = P + SI

💰 Compound Interest
A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ
CI = A − P
✅ P=10000, R=10%, n=2 → A=12100, CI=₹2100
📌 CI > SI (except 1st year). Banks use CI!

⭕ Circle Formulas
Area = πr²
Circumference = 2πr
✅ r=7 → Area = 3.14×49 = 153.86 sq units
Circumference = 2×3.14×7 = 43.96 units

🔺 Triangles
By sides: Equilateral(3=), Isosceles(2=), Scalene(all≠)
By angles: Acute(<90°), Right(=90°), Obtuse(>90°)
Area = ½ × base × height
📌 Sum of all angles = 180° always!

% Percentage
% = (Part/Whole) × 100
Increase%: ((New−Old)/Old)×100
✅ 40 out of 50 → (40/50)×100 = 80%
📌 Used in profit/loss, marks, growth!

🔢 LCM & HCF
HCF = Greatest common factor
LCM = Least common multiple
LCM × HCF = Product of two numbers
✅ 12 & 18: HCF=6, LCM=36 → 6×36=216=12×18 ✓
📌 Use prime factorization method!

🔣 Key Algebraic Identities
(a+b)² = a²+2ab+b²
(a−b)² = a²−2ab+b²
(a+b)(a−b) = a²−b²
(a+b)³ = a³+3a²b+3ab²+b³
📌 Memorise these — they appear everywhere in algebra!

📊 Mean, Median & Mode
Mean = Sum of values ÷ Count
Median = Middle value (sorted list)
Mode = Most frequent value
✅ Data: 2,3,3,5,7 → Mean=4, Median=3, Mode=3
📌 For even count: Median = avg of 2 middle values

🛒 Profit & Loss
Profit = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP
Profit% = (Profit/CP)×100
Discount% = (Discount/MP)×100
✅ CP=200, SP=250 → Profit=50, Profit%=25%

⚖️ Ratio & Proportion
Ratio a:b = a/b
Direct: y∝x → y=kx (both increase together)
Inverse: y∝1/x → xy=k (one increases, other decreases)
✅ 5 pens cost ₹25 → 8 pens = ₹40 (direct)

📏 Linear Equations
1 variable: ax + b = 0 → x = −b/a
2 variables: Use substitution or elimination
✅ 2x + 3 = 11 → 2x = 8 → x = 4
📌 Linear means highest power of variable = 1

📦 3D Geometry Formulas
Cube: Volume=a³, SA=6a²
Cuboid: Volume=l×b×h, SA=2(lb+bh+lh)
Cylinder: Volume=πr²h, CSA=2πrh
Sphere: Volume=4/3πr³, SA=4πr²
📌 Learn these for board exams!

🌿 Photosynthesis
6CO₂ + 6H₂O + sunlight → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
📌 Occurs in chloroplasts (chlorophyll pigment)
Light reaction: thylakoid (ATP produced)
Dark reaction: stroma (glucose produced)
Output: Glucose (food) + Oxygen released

🍎 Newton's 3 Laws of Motion
1️⃣ Inertia: Object stays at rest/motion unless external force acts
2️⃣ F = ma: Force = mass × acceleration
3️⃣ Action–Reaction: Every action → equal & opposite reaction
✅ Rocket launch = Law 3! Walking = Law 3!

⚡ Ohm's Law
V = I × R
V=Voltage(V), I=Current(A), R=Resistance(Ω)
✅ V=12V, R=4Ω → I = 12/4 = 3 Amperes
📌 More resistance → less current. Series: R total = R1+R2

🔬 Mitosis (Cell Division)
Remember: PMAT
P → Prophase (chromosomes condense & become visible)
M → Metaphase (line up at cell equator)
A → Anaphase (sister chromatids pulled apart)
T → Telophase (nuclear envelope reforms)
Result: 2 identical daughter cells (same DNA)

⚗️ Periodic Table
118 elements | 7 periods | 18 groups
Group 1 = Alkali metals | Group 17 = Halogens | Group 18 = Noble gases
Metals (left) | Non-metals (right) | Metalloids (staircase)
📌 Atomic number = protons | Mass number = protons + neutrons

🧪 Acids & Bases
Acid: pH < 7 (HCl, H₂SO₄, vinegar, lemon)
Base: pH > 7 (NaOH, NH₃, soap, baking soda)
Neutral: pH = 7 (pure water)
Neutralization: Acid + Base → Salt + Water
📌 Litmus: red in acid, blue in base

🌍 Gravitation
F = Gm₁m₂/r²
G = 6.67×10⁻¹¹ Nm²/kg²
g (Earth) = 9.8 m/s²
📌 Weight = mass × g
Moon g = Earth g / 6 (you weigh less on moon!)
Free fall: all objects fall at same rate (ignoring air resistance)

🔊 Sound Waves
Speed in air ≈ 343 m/s (at 20°C)
Speed order: solid > liquid > gas
v = fλ (velocity = frequency × wavelength)
Ultrasound: >20,000 Hz (medical imaging)
Infrasound: <20 Hz
📌 Sound needs a medium — cannot travel in vacuum!

💡 Light & Optics
Speed of light = 3×10⁸ m/s (vacuum)
Reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection
Snell's Law: n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂
Convex lens: converging | Concave lens: diverging
📌 Rainbow = dispersion of white light by water droplets!

🌱 Ecosystem & Food Chain
Producers → Primary Consumers → Secondary → Tertiary
(Plants → Herbivores → Carnivores → Top predators)
Energy transfer: only 10% moves to next trophic level
📌 Decomposers (fungi/bacteria) recycle nutrients back to soil

🫀 Human Body Systems
🫁 Respiratory: lungs exchange O₂/CO₂
❤️ Circulatory: heart pumps blood (~72 bpm)
🍽️ Digestive: mouth → stomach → small intestine → large intestine
🧠 Nervous: brain + spinal cord + nerves
📌 206 bones | 37 trillion cells | Largest organ = skin!

⚡ Electricity
Series: same current, voltages add: R_total = R1+R2
Parallel: same voltage, currents add: 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2
Power P = VI = I²R = V²/R
✅ P = 10V × 2A = 20 Watts
📌 1 kWh = 1 unit of electricity (billing unit)

⚛️ Atoms & Molecules
Atom: protons + neutrons (nucleus) + electrons (shells)
Shell capacity: K=2, L=8, M=18
Valency = electrons needed to complete outer shell
Ionic bond: electron transfer | Covalent bond: electron sharing
📌 NaCl = ionic | H₂O = covalent

🚀 Force & Motion
Speed = Distance/Time
Velocity = Displacement/Time (has direction)
Acceleration = (v−u)/t
KE = ½mv² | PE = mgh
📌 Work = Force × Distance (unit: Joule)
Power = Work/Time (unit: Watt)

📝 8 Parts of Speech
1. Noun – name (Delhi, book, joy)
2. Pronoun – replaces noun (he, she, they)
3. Verb – action/state (run, is, feels)
4. Adjective – describes noun (big, red, happy)
5. Adverb – modifies verb (quickly, very)
6. Preposition – position (in, on, at, under)
7. Conjunction – joins (and, but, or, because)
8. Interjection – emotion (Wow! Oh! Ouch!)

⏱ 12 Tenses (3×4)
Present: Simple | Continuous | Perfect | Perfect Continuous
Past: Simple | Continuous | Perfect | Perfect Continuous
Future: Simple | Continuous | Perfect | Perfect Continuous
✅ I eat (Simple Present) | I am eating (Present Continuous) | I have eaten (Present Perfect)

🗣️ Active vs Passive Voice
Active: Subject → Verb → Object
'The dog bit the man.'
Passive: Object → be+V3 → by+Subject
'The man was bitten by the dog.'
📌 Passive formula = is/am/are/was/were + V3
Use passive when doer is unknown or unimportant

✍️ Figures of Speech
🔸 Simile: like/as → 'brave as a lion'
🔸 Metaphor: direct → 'life is a journey'
🔸 Personification: 'the wind whispered'
🔸 Hyperbole: 'I've told you a million times'
🔸 Alliteration: 'Peter Piper picked...'
🔸 Onomatopoeia: sound words → buzz, splash, hiss

✏️ Essay Writing Structure
📌 Introduction (3–4 lines): Hook + Background + Thesis
📌 Body (2–3 paragraphs): Topic sentence + Evidence + Explanation
📌 Conclusion: Restate thesis + Summary + Closing thought
💡 Linking words: Furthermore, However, Therefore, In conclusion, Nevertheless

📜 Types of Sentences
By structure:
• Simple (1 clause) | Compound (2 independent) | Complex (1 independent + 1 dependent)
By purpose:
• Declarative: She reads books.
• Interrogative: Does she read?
• Imperative: Read this!
• Exclamatory: What a book!

🔤 Punctuation Guide
, Comma – pause, list, clauses
. Full stop – end of sentence
; Semicolon – join related clauses
: Colon – introduce list/explanation
' Apostrophe – possession (cat's) or contraction (don't)
" " Quotes – direct speech
📌 Common mistake: its (possession) vs it's (it is)

📖 Comprehension Strategy
1. Skim the passage first (30 sec overview)
2. Read all questions carefully
3. Re-read passage for specific answers
4. Answer in your own words (unless asked to quote)
5. Never leave blanks — attempt every question!
📌 Marks for comprehension are easy to score — be thorough!

📚 Key Synonyms & Antonyms
Beautiful ↔ Ugly (Gorgeous, Pretty)
Brave ↔ Cowardly (Courageous, Bold)
Ancient ↔ Modern (Old, Archaic)
Transparent ↔ Opaque (Clear, Obvious)
Abundant ↔ Scarce (Plentiful, Ample)
📌 Build vocabulary: learn 5 new words daily — it's a game changer!

📮 Letter Writing Format
Formal Letter:
Sender's address → Date → Receiver's address → Subject → Salutation (Dear Sir/Ma'am) → Body (3 para) → Closing (Yours faithfully) → Signature
Informal Letter:
Sender's address → Date → Salutation (Dear friend) → Body → Closing (Yours lovingly)
📌 Subject line is mandatory in formal letters!

💬 Direct & Indirect Speech
Direct: He said, "I am happy."
Indirect: He said that he was happy.
Tense changes: am→was, is→was, will→would, can→could
Pronoun changes: I→he/she, we→they, my→his/her
📌 Remove comma and quotation marks in indirect!
